claims.text: The starting material is additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy has an fcc matrix.
Formation of a thermally grown oxide layer governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases.
Catastrophic failure occurs when the TGO reaches a critical thickness.
Reaching the critical TGO thickness causes oxide spallation.
TGO spallation exposes the underlying alloy to the corrosive gas and thereby promotes catastrophic degradation.
Temperature and gas composition control oxidation and corrosion through thermodynamic and kinetic effects on TGO formation and spallation.
The proposed applicable exposure range is 700–1000 °C for 100 hours in air, Ar-20%O2, or Ar-5%H2.
Exposure to air at 900 °C will increase the degradation rate by 30% relative to the starting-state baseline.
Exposure to Ar-5%H2 at 800 °C will decrease the degradation rate by 50% relative to the starting-state baseline.
The critical TGO thickness may depend on exposure conditions.
A critical TGO thickness of 10 μm is used as a falsification threshold.
The hypothesis is falsified if degradation in air at 900 °C does not increase by at least 20%.
The hypothesis is falsified if the TGO does not reach 10 μm thickness.

contradictions.description: The critical TGO thickness is said to be unknown and exposure-dependent, yet 10 μm is treated as a fixed critical value without evidence or a stated calibration procedure.
